axis_A_basis: 2 trials in this review (SELECT n=17604; Wilson tirzepatide n=316)
axis_B_source: Plutzky 2026 Circulation PMID 42610271 (PMC13574348)
axis_B_detail: Baseline predicts MACE HR 2.17 (1.81-2.58), CV death 3.94 (3.04-5.08), all-cause death 3.40 (2.77-4.14) for >=10 vs <2 mg/L. Treatment-induced change predicts outcome: adjusting for time-varying hsCRP attenuated MACE HR from 0.80 to 0.86, marking ~32% of effect. Effect homogeneous across LDL, statin use, BMI and baseline hsCRP strata; cohort 88% statin use, median LDL 78 mg/dL.
assessor_note: Highest graded marker in the inventory. Mediation analysis within the same trial population is what B1 requires and it is present. adj+ granted: effect shown independent of LDL, statin use and BMI strata, and change-in-hsCRP analysis adjusted for baseline LDL and statin use.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Wilson tirzepatide n=316; Konstantinidou liraglutide). Note between-group contrasts were NOT significant; within-arm only
axis_B_source: Nopp 2021 Eur J Intern Med PMID 33706979; Nopp 2023 J Thromb Haemost PMID 37192696
axis_B_detail: Predicts all-cause mortality and MACE in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, adjusted HR 2.33 per doubling (1.74-3.13) for death and 2.33 (1.60-3.39) for MACE, n=362. Predicts all-cause death in cancer cohort adjusted HR 1.21 per doubling (1.10-1.33), n=1531. Basis of the validated ABC-death score, C-statistic 0.80.
assessor_note: Graded B3 not B2 because of POPULATION MISMATCH. The prediction evidence comes from atrial fibrillation and cancer cohorts; the drug-response evidence comes from obesity and T2D trials. These are not comparable populations on age, adiposity or disease status, so the criteria do not permit B2. No study has tested whether treatment-induced GDF-15 change predicts outcome in any population. GDF-15 also rises with metformin and with cancer cachexia, so its direction of clinical meaning in a weight-loss context is not established and may differ from its meaning as a stress marker.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci survodutide, both arms; also Ren 2025 meta-analysis SMD +0.69 across GLP-1 RAs)
axis_B_source: Wu 2014 Metabolism PMID 24933398 (meta-analysis, 14063 CVD patients, 15 cohorts); Yang 2025 Metabolites PMID 40278358 (CKD meta-analysis, 2523 patients)
axis_B_detail: DIRECTION CONFLICT. Higher adiponectin predicts HIGHER mortality in established CVD: all-cause HR 1.45 (1.17-1.79) and CV death HR 1.69 (1.35-2.10) for highest vs lowest tertile across 14063 patients. Same paradoxical direction in CKD with BMI >=25 (HR 1.023 per ug/mL). The review assumes higher adiponectin is favourable; the outcome data in the population most comparable to SELECT (established ASCVD) say the opposite.
assessor_note: GRADED WITH A DIRECTION DISCORDANCE FLAG. The drug raises adiponectin and the composite scores that as favourable (direction +1). In CVD cohorts, which is the SELECT population, higher adiponectin predicts death. Wu et al note the association may be amplified by adjustment for intermediates or by residual confounding, and the mechanistic view is that adiponectin rises compensatorily in heart failure and cachexia. But the surrogacy question is whether the marker predicts outcomes in the right direction in the treated population, and here it does not. The composite's adiponectin contribution of roughly +9 pct harmonised should be treated as unvalidated in direction, not merely in magnitude. This is the first marker where the assumed aging direction is contradicted by outcome data and it must be reported.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial here (Wilson tirzepatide); also Ren 2025 meta-analysis SMD -0.67 across GLP-1 RAs
axis_B_source: Kord-Varkaneh 2018 Horm Metab Res PMID 29991082 (meta-analysis, 19 studies, 16208 subjects for all-cause mortality)
axis_B_detail: NO overall association with all-cause mortality: HR 1.028 (0.908-1.165), p=0.659, I2=61%. Subgroups show higher leptin associated with higher mortality in healthy people (HR 1.159), men (1.162) and age >=60 (1.129), but LOWER cancer mortality (HR 0.550). No evidence located in an obesity or T2D treated population, and no mediation evidence anywhere.
assessor_note: Graded B4 not B3. The pooled result is null and the subgroup findings point in opposite directions by population, which is weaker than a consistent cohort association. Leptin falls mechanically with fat mass, so in a weight loss trial it is close to a restatement of the weight change rather than an independent aging signal. Of all markers in the inventory this is the one most likely to be a weight proxy, and the adj qualifier cannot even be applied because no B1 or B2 evidence exists to adjust.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial here (Wilson tirzepatide, unchanged in all arms); Ren 2025 meta-analysis SMD -0.76; Alrasheed 2026 SMD -0.24 vs insulin only
axis_B_source: IL6R Mendelian Randomisation Analysis Consortium 2012 Lancet PMID 22421340 (PMC3316968), 40 studies up to 133449 individuals, 25458 CHD cases
axis_B_detail: CAUSAL genetic evidence. IL6R variant rs7529229 associated with decreased odds of coronary heart disease, OR 0.95 per allele (0.93-0.97), p=1.5e-5. The variant's biomarker signature (higher circulating IL-6, lower CRP and fibrinogen) matches the pattern produced by tocilizumab in RCTs, which validates the instrument against a pharmacological intervention on the same target.
assessor_note: The ONLY marker in the inventory with human genetic causal evidence, which is why grade B0 was added. Two cautions that matter more than the grade. First, the causal evidence is for IL-6 RECEPTOR SIGNALLING, not for circulating IL-6 concentration; the MR variant RAISES circulating IL-6 while blocking signalling, so lowering measured IL-6 is not the same intervention as blocking the pathway and the direction of benefit does not transfer straightforwardly. Second, this drug class barely moves it: unchanged in every arm of Wilson, and significant in Alrasheed only against insulin. A causally important pathway that the drug does not meaningfully alter is not evidence of an anti-aging effect, and presenting B0 beside a null drug effect without that caveat would be misleading.

axis_A_basis: Not in our extraction but established class-wide: Nong 2026 BMJ 262-trial NMA, tirzepatide lean mass -8.3 pct; Locatelli 2024 Diabetes Care
axis_B_source: Antoniou 2019 Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg PMID 31204184 (meta-analysis, 7 cohorts, 1440 patients); Sun 2026 Curr Med Chem PMID 41863167 (chronic HF, 1209 patients plus meta-analysis)
axis_B_detail: Low skeletal muscle mass predicts all-cause mortality after abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, HR 1.66 (1.15-2.40). Low sarcopenia index associated with all-cause mortality in chronic heart failure, OR 0.42 (0.28-0.62) for high vs low. Both are surgical or heart failure populations, not obesity.
assessor_note: THE ONLY MARKER IN THE INVENTORY MOVING UNFAVOURABLY, and the one where the surrogacy question is most consequential. Graded B3 on population mismatch: the mortality evidence comes from AAA surgery and heart failure cohorts where low muscle mass reflects cachexia and frailty, not from people losing weight on a GLP-1 agonist. Whether drug-induced lean mass loss in a person with obesity carries the same prognostic meaning as sarcopenia in a frail surgical patient is UNKNOWN and is the central unresolved safety question for this drug class. Linge 2024 Circulation distinguishes adaptive from maladaptive muscle change, which is precisely the distinction the cohort literature cannot make. No trial has tested whether treatment-induced lean mass loss predicts any outcome. This absence should be stated as the inventory's most important evidence gap, ahead of the missing GDF-15 data.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci survodutide both trials); widely reported class-wide
axis_B_source: No adequately adjusted prospective outcome study located in a treated population. Insulin resistance is strongly associated with incident diabetes and CVD, but HOMA-IR specifically has not been shown to predict hard outcomes independent of the components used to compute it (fasting glucose and insulin).
axis_B_detail: HOMA-IR is a derived index, not a measured analyte: it is a function of fasting glucose and fasting insulin, both of which are separately in this inventory. Treating it as an independent biomarker double counts those two. In a composite it should either replace its components or be excluded, not sit alongside them. No mediation evidence exists.
assessor_note: Flagged for a structural problem beyond its grade. HOMA-IR = (fasting glucose x fasting insulin)/22.5. Including it in the composite alongside fasting glucose and fasting insulin counts the same information up to three times and inflates the nutrient sensing domain's weight. This must be resolved before any NBAIS is computed. Recommend retaining HOMA-IR and dropping its two components, since the index is the interpretable quantity.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci survodutide; significant in T2D trial only)
axis_B_source: Searched: no prospective study located linking HOMA-beta to a hard outcome in any population.
axis_B_detail: Beta cell function indices predict glycaemic deterioration and progression to insulin requirement, which are intermediate outcomes, not hard outcomes under these criteria. Same derived-index problem as HOMA-IR.
assessor_note: B5 means searched and nothing located, not unsearched. Also a derived index sharing inputs with fasting glucose and fasting insulin.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci both trials, highly significant)
axis_B_source: Extensive prospective literature links fasting glucose to CVD and mortality; however no study located that tests whether TREATMENT-INDUCED change in fasting glucose predicts outcome change in this drug class.
axis_B_detail: Baseline fasting glucose predicts hard outcomes in populations comparable to these trials. But the surrogacy failure of glycaemic control is the best documented in cardiovascular medicine: ACCORD, ADVANCE and VADT each lowered glucose without the expected outcome benefit, and ACCORD increased mortality.
assessor_note: adj- because the association is rarely adjusted for adiposity. More importantly this marker carries a documented SURROGACY FAILURE. Lowering glucose has repeatedly failed to deliver the outcome benefit its epidemiology predicted. Any composite that treats a glucose reduction as evidence of slowed biological aging is making exactly the inference that ACCORD refuted. This must be stated explicitly in the manuscript.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci; significant in obesity trial only)
axis_B_source: Searched: hyperinsulinaemia associated with incident diabetes and CVD in cohorts, but adjusted independent prediction of hard outcomes is inconsistent and assay standardisation is poor.
axis_B_detail: No mediation evidence. Component of HOMA-IR, see double counting note.
assessor_note: Insulin assays are not standardised across laboratories, which limits cross-trial comparability independent of the surrogacy question.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci; significant in obesity trial only)
axis_B_source: Searched: C-peptide associates with CVD in some cohorts, direction inconsistent, and it is largely a marker of endogenous insulin secretion rather than an aging process.
axis_B_detail: No mediation evidence located.
assessor_note: Weak conceptual claim to being an aging biomarker at all. Recommend considering removal from the inventory on face validity grounds rather than on evidence grounds.

axis_A_basis: 2 trials (Ekinci both, highly significant)
axis_B_source: Searched: no prospective outcome study located linking circulating glucagon to hard outcomes.
axis_B_detail: Glucagon reduction here is a target engagement marker for GCGR agonism, not an aging signal.
assessor_note: Recommend reclassifying glucagon as a pharmacodynamic target engagement marker and REMOVING it from the aging biomarker inventory. It currently contributes 8.4 percent of the harmonised composite weight despite having no claim to being an aging biomarker. Retaining it would be indefensible to a geroscience reviewer.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Wilson tirzepatide, -41.6 pct, p<0.001 vs placebo and dulaglutide)
axis_B_source: Searched: YKL-40 (chitinase 3 like protein 1) predicts all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in general population cohorts, notably the Copenhagen City Heart Study lineage.
axis_B_detail: No study located testing treatment-induced YKL-40 change against outcomes, and no evidence in an obesity or T2D treated population.
assessor_note: One of the larger drug effects in the inventory and among the better supported inflammatory markers after hsCRP. Worth noting that YKL-40 is strongly elevated by any inflammatory or malignant process, so specificity for aging is poor.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Wilson tirzepatide, -9.6 pct)
axis_B_source: Searched: soluble ICAM-1 predicts incident coronary events in cohorts, with attenuation after adjustment for conventional risk factors in several studies.
axis_B_detail: No mediation evidence. Effect size in our data is modest.
assessor_note: Prediction is inconsistent after adjustment, which places it at the weaker end of B3.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Wilson tirzepatide, +6.9 pct, not significant in any arm)
axis_B_source: NT-proBNP is among the best validated prognostic markers in cardiovascular medicine, predicting mortality and heart failure hospitalisation across broad populations including those with obesity, with adjustment for standard risk factors.
axis_B_detail: Strong prediction, but the drug does not move it: no significant change in any arm of the only trial reporting it.
assessor_note: An instructive cell. NT-proBNP has the second strongest outcome prediction evidence in the inventory and is the only marker where the point estimate is unfavourable, yet the effect is null. It should be reported as a validated marker showing no benefit rather than quietly dropped, because a selectively reported panel that omits validated nulls is the reporting bias this review's own Methods warn about.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Sanyal retatrutide, -82.7 pct)
axis_B_source: Searched: hepatic steatosis by imaging associates with incident cardiovascular events and mortality in cohorts, but associations attenuate substantially after adjustment for metabolic confounders, and steatosis without fibrosis carries limited prognostic weight.
axis_B_detail: Fibrosis stage, not steatosis, is the hepatic feature that predicts liver related and all cause mortality. PDFF measures steatosis.
assessor_note: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION. The hepatic literature is clear that FIBROSIS predicts outcomes and steatosis largely does not once fibrosis is accounted for. Our largest single effect in the entire inventory, -82.7 pct liver fat, is on the feature with the weaker prognostic claim. The review should not present hepatic fat reduction as an aging benefit without stating this.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Meyhofer SELECT, -1.9 U/L)
axis_B_source: Searched: ALT has a U-shaped association with mortality, with LOW ALT associated with frailty and increased mortality in older adults. Elevated ALT associates with liver related mortality.
axis_B_detail: Baseline ALT in SELECT was within the normal range, so the direction of benefit from lowering it is not established.
assessor_note: The U-shaped association matters here. SELECT lowered ALT from a baseline already within normal limits, and low ALT is a recognised frailty marker in older adults. Lowering a normal ALT should not be scored as an aging benefit without acknowledging this.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Meyhofer SELECT, -0.9 U/L)
axis_B_source: Searched: same U-shaped pattern as ALT; AST alone is a weak prognostic marker.
axis_B_detail: Baseline within normal range.
assessor_note: Same caveat as ALT.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Meyhofer SELECT, -8.2 U/L, 17 pct relative, the largest of the three enzymes)
axis_B_source: Searched: GGT predicts all cause and cardiovascular mortality in large general population cohorts with a monotonic dose response, and is the best validated of the three liver enzymes for this purpose.
axis_B_detail: No mediation evidence in a treated population.
assessor_note: Of the three transaminases GGT has the strongest and most consistent outcome prediction, and it also showed the largest relative change. Worth highlighting over ALT and AST rather than treating the three as equivalent.

axis_A_basis: 1 trial (Meyhofer SELECT, -16.1 points)
axis_B_source: Searched: FLI predicts incident diabetes and some cardiovascular outcomes, but it is a composite computed from BMI, waist circumference, triglycerides and GGT.
axis_B_detail: Not an independent measurement.
assessor_note: STRUCTURAL PROBLEM. FLI is computed from BMI and waist circumference, so it is substantially a restatement of adiposity. Including it in a composite that is then tested for weight independence is close to circular. Recommend excluding FLI from the composite and reporting it descriptively only.
